pages.note: 18 November 2026: first published. Every colour value is rendered from docs/data/govuk-brand-colours.json, copied verbatim from the GOV.UK Brand Guidelines maps page read on 18 November 2026 (Open Government Licence v3.0), including the colours of the GOV.UK map example under pages.maps.example. Map colours are the same in light and dark mode and do not follow the theme colour. 18 November 2026 (GOV.UK layout): swatches now use the GOV.UK Brand layout, the page lists its colour groups, and the zones drawing is shown on the page with its key, invented-data note and data table (in a details element), followed by Colours used in example. 18 November 2026 (Home Assistant rewrite, round 2): the page names no outside source. Each colour in the working OpenStreetMap example is tied to a feature you can see (roads, buildings, Roath Basin, markers A and B), with a colour key below the map; rivers are described as low-contrast Teal tint 80% lines; zones and markers use one data colour and are told apart by shape, letter and label. In Home Assistant now says the native Map card can take these colours through a custom map_style with colors and colors_dark, and links to Maps, zones and location records for attribution. The shared map example has a shorter description and a plain caption. The shared example disclaimer was replaced by one invented-data statement per example. 18 November 2026 (final gate fixes): the scale bar was moved clear of the in-map attribution at 320px in commit 5e8b7a1. In Home Assistant now says a custom map_style colours only the base map (its colour keys, from @versatiles/style, name base-map features only) and that Accent green zones and markers apply to maps you draw yourself. White was added to the base map swatches and the repeated colour list under the working example became one sentence. The zones drawing scales to the page width with 28px labels, has one invented-data statement (in the caption) and no longer repeats its colours in the frame. The headings are now Example: zones on a base map and Colours used in the example (check-colours.mjs updated to match). In Home Assistant states the native zone and marker colours (Home zone primary-color, passive zones secondary-text-color, others color-N in creation order), checked against frontend commit b1164739.
pages.title: Map colours

pages.note: 18 November 2026: first published. Every palette value is rendered from docs/data/govuk-brand-colours.json, and the example tiles are generated from it by docs/scripts/generate-social-examples.py; the values were copied verbatim from the GOV.UK Brand Guidelines social page read on 18 November 2026 (Open Government Licence v3.0), including the 9 companion pairings under pages.social.companion. Social colours do not follow the theme colour and are not used in the Home Assistant interface. 18 November 2026 (GOV.UK layout): swatches now use the GOV.UK Brand layout, the page lists its colour groups, the tone tiles sit on an Inform to Inspire scale, and each tonal and companion example tile has its own heading and the swatches of the colours it uses; maintenance notes moved to Colour. 18 November 2026 (Home Assistant rewrite, round 2): the page names no outside source. Tonal and companion colours are defined where first used; the tonal tiles carry serious messages in one colour family each (the red tile text is now Red tint 95%, 4.79:1; the green tile circle is Green tint 80%); the palette is described as the app palette without the dark mode blues; repeated sentences were removed. 18 November 2026 (final gate fixes): the tone strip wraps on narrow screens and its text no longer shrinks to about 3px at 320px (commit 5e8b7a1). The tone order is described as first to last rather than left to right. The contrast bullet links to Test combinations and keep another cue instead of naming an outside standard. The Primary yellow companion tile now reads See where your energy goes, an Energy dashboard action.

examples.title: A text-first report that separates recent, old and absent readings
examples.review_note: Freshness distinguishes two recent readings, one older reading and one unconfigured room. The 2-of-3 configured denominator and all four room records are explicit, with no fabricated diagnosis or physical controls.

examples.title: Four room humidity lines in the civica chart colours, in light and dark mode
examples.review_note: 18 November 2026 redraw: a line chart of synthetic relative humidity in 4 rooms over one day, in light and dark mode, coloured civica-chart-1 to civica-chart-4 from themes/civica.yaml in order, as a History graph card colours them. Final-gate redraw (18 November 2026): solid lines and a legend only, as a native History graph card draws them, with no dashes, markers or end labels; the living room's missing readings are a gap with 'No data' and 'Not supplied' in the table. Low-contrast colours on the dark card are named once on the Chart colours page. The caption carries one synthetic-data statement and no page rules. Generated by docs/scripts/generate-data-colour-examples.py.

examples.title: Sequential and divergent heatmaps with explicit missing data
examples.review_note: 18 November 2026 redraw: two heatmaps of synthetic data for 5 rooms over 9 to 15 November 2026. Daily energy (kWh) on 5 listed Blues steps of 0.4 kWh with a supplied zero in the lightest step; difference from a 20 °C target on Blues and Reds with Black tint 95% at the centre. Every cell prints its value in Black or White at 4.5:1 or more, missing readings are crossed empty cells, boundary and out-of-range rules are stated, and matching tables give every value. Generated by docs/scripts/generate-data-colour-examples.py.

examples.title: Single category bar chart
examples.review_note: Like-for-like with the GOV.UK "Single category" chart composition: synthetic daily electricity use (kWh) as bars in Primary blue, Black tint 80% grid lines and Black labels. Labelled synthetic data, period, unit, source, value labels on bars and a matching table.

examples.title: Multiple categories line chart
examples.review_note: Four synthetic room temperatures as lines coloured civica-chart-1 to civica-chart-4 in legend order (Primary blue, Primary magenta, Teal tint 25%, Blue shade 50%; recoloured 18 November 2026 from an out-of-order set), each with its own dash and an end label, legend on top and a matching table. 18 November 2026 final gate: removed the repeated sentence that the values are readings at a moment.

examples.title: Divergent stacked bar chart
examples.review_note: Like-for-like with the GOV.UK "Divergent categories" composition: synthetic hours under and over the heating target per room in Primary blue, Blue tint 50%, Red tint 50% and Primary red, legend on top, position as a non-colour cue and a matching table including hours on target.

examples.title: Social media chart
examples.review_note: Synthetic automation counts as area-sized circles on Blue shade 50% with Accent teal and Teal tint 95%, used only on that shade background. Values are printed on every circle and repeated in a table. 18 November 2026: the drawn example label and the drawn data note were removed; the caption carries the one simulation statement.

examples.title: A selected entity and a separate provider

examples.title: Storage observations without a recovery guarantee
examples.review_note: 64 GiB total and 18 GiB available are labelled binary units; unavailable share is not zero. Capacity does not imply backup restorability; diagnostic redaction is specific.

examples.title: A technical All result is not physical confirmation
examples.review_note: All-with-only-unavailable-targets is explicitly the native technical condition rule and not a claim that windows are closed; current official targets documentation was read to verify the surprising result.

examples.title: Mode, current action and temperature are different
examples.review_note: Heat mode, Heating action, current 19.5 °C and target 21 °C are different fields; source does not conflate mode with activity.

examples.title: The same raw state can have different meanings
examples.review_note: Binary-sensor on is mapped to Open, Detected and Low by device-class context; each exact label was confirmed against the source register.

examples.title: One device, two different entities
examples.review_note: A device versus two entities is clear; 0 W and reported Off remain separate, supplied apostrophe and literal IDs preserved, time context explicit.

examples.title: An event and an action describe different things
examples.review_note: Triggered event, condition and requested operation are separate. Local-only outline review does not claim an automation was saved or run.

examples.title: Explain an older name while preserving a literal path

examples.title: Explain an identifier without changing it

examples.title: Missing states and an old report need different wording

examples.title: Keep the native label, explain it nearby

examples.title: A Home Assistant dashboard in the web palette
examples.review_note: 18 November 2026 redraw: the picture is now drawn as Home Assistant looks with the civica theme, not modelled on an outside picture. A desktop browser shows Home Assistant’s own sidebar (the civica companion’s Primary blue menu row with the unchanged civica lock-up, Overview, Energy, Map, Logbook, History, Settings, Notifications and the user), the Primary blue toolbar with the view tabs Home, Upstairs and Garden (Home Assistant shows tabs instead of a title when a dashboard has more than one view), and on a White background 2 badges, an entities card with civica switches, a thermostat card in heat mode, sensor tiles and a markdown card with a link. The Menu button, the Blue tint 95% page and the Blue tint 50% backdrop are gone. Colours follow themes/civica.yaml light mode; the selected sidebar row (#E8EEF3) and its text (#19578D) are not palette colours, so Black tint 95% and Blue shade 25% stand in, and Home Assistant’s own heating orange is drawn as Primary orange. Every fill and stroke is a web palette colour and every text pair reaches 4.5:1, checked by docs/scripts/generate-web-app-examples.py. The picture scrolls sideways in a focusable region on screens narrower than 600px so that its text stays readable; checked at 1280px and 320px.
